thread:
alex_acme: Hey team — after switching to poetry for our service, importing the Python SDK fails in our container. Error on startup: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood.client'`. We installed via `poetry add redwood` (v1.2.0).

jess_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact install commands and a quick `pip list` from the venv/container? Also which python version?

alex_acme: python 3.10.6, container is Debian slim. Steps we ran:
```
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
poetry init --no-interaction
poetry add redwood==1.2.0
poetry install --no-root
```
`pip list` shows: `redwood 1.2.0`, `httpx 0.19.0`, `httpcore 0.12.0`

jess_support: Ah, two quick things to check: 1) if you rely on async features the SDK's async client comes from extras (e.g. `redwood[async]`) — poetry won't add extras unless you specify them. 2) older httpx/httpcore can change import paths; our async client expects httpx>=0.23. Can you try `python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__file__)"` and also `python -c "import importlib; print(importlib.util.find_spec('redwood.client'))"`?

alex_acme: Running that shows `redwood` package path points to `/app/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py` and `find_spec('redwood.client')` is None.

ian_devex: Two likely causes: (A) The package was installed without extras so the subpackage providing `client` wasn't pulled in, or (B) there was an editable/local install that shadowed the wheel. Another clue is the old httpx version in your pip list. If you used a `pyproject` that pins an httpx older than 0.23, poetry may have resolved an incompatible set.

alex_acme: We are also doing a local editable install earlier in our Dockerfile: `pip install -e .` (we copy source into /app first). Could that be the culprit?

jess_support: Yes — `pip install -e .` will not install extras unless you do `pip install -e '.[async]'`. If your package has a local `redwood` directory (for a different internal package) it can shadow the installed SDK. Two immediate repro steps: 1) in the venv run `python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__path__)"` to confirm source vs site-packages; 2) try reinstalling the SDK explicitly with extras: `pip install --upgrade 'redwood[async]>=1.2.0'` or with poetry `poetry add "redwood[async]@1.2.0"`.

alex_acme: Tried `pip install --upgrade 'redwood[async]>=1.2.0'` — pip upgraded httpx to 0.23.3 and httpcore to 0.23.x. After that `import redwood.client` still fails. `redwood.__path__` prints `/app/src/redwood` (our local package).

ian_devex: Bingo — your repo has a top-level package named `redwood` (internal helper) that is shadowing the SDK. That's why `find_spec('redwood.client')` is None — the local package doesn't expose that submodule. Two options: rename your local package, or vendor the SDK under a different import name. Common workaround in Docker: install the SDK into the environment before copying your source, or install editable with the extras: `pip install -e '.[async]'` after copying so the SDK takes precedence in site-packages.

alex_acme: Ugh, we do have an internal `redwood/` dir. We renamed it to `acme_redwood` locally and adjusted imports; rebuilt container and now `import redwood.client` works — thanks.

jess_support: Great. As a follow-up: if you ever need both packages named similarly, you can also use an explicit vendor import (not ideal). Also watch for poetry lock conflicts — if pyproject pins older httpx, upgrade that constraint. For reproducibility, add `httpx = ">=0.23"` to your pyproject or run `poetry add "httpx@^0.23"` and then `poetry lock && poetry install`.

alex_acme: Will do. One more small note for the team: in Dockerfile we now install sdk before copying app to avoid shadowing.

deploy-bot: Deployment succeeded for acme/staging at rev abc123 (after rebuild). :thumbsup:

jess_support: Thanks for the debug info — marking this resolved. :white_check_mark:
